subject: Renewal pricing pathway & usage cushion — SolarCog
messages:
From: Tanya Rosales <tanya@solarcog.com>
To: david_kim@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@solarcog.com
Date: Mon, 01 Oct 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal planning — capacity uplift and price hold

David / Monica,

We're coming up on our 12-month renewal and we'd like to start discussion early. Our product usage has climbed steadily and we expect to need ~30% more committed capacity next year. High level asks from SolarCog: 

- Can we convert our current retainer to a committed monthly baseline (30% uplift) with a 12-month price hold?
- We'd like a short-term surge cushion for the first 90 days post-renewal (we anticipate a spike from a new feature rollout).
- Procurement will want a clear articulation of overage rates, SLA credits, and any credit or incentive we can attach to a multi-quarter commit.

I've looped in procurement (Ethan) — they'll require a redline-able SOW. Attaching last quarter's usage extract for reference.

Attachment: solarcog_q3_usage.csv (summary)

Best,
Tanya
VP Product — SolarCog
From: david_kim@redwood.ai
To: Tanya Rosales <tanya@solarcog.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 02 Oct 2028 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — capacity uplift and price hold

Tanya — thanks for the early heads up, this is perfect timing. I'm proposing two clean pathways so procurement and engineering can pick the risk profile that fits SolarCog: 

Option A — Commit-forward (recommended for predictability):
- Convert current retainer into a 12-month committed baseline with a 30% uplift in reserved tokens/embeddings.
- Price hold: maintain today's effective blended rate for 12 months on the existing baseline; incremental capacity above baseline receives a 10% discount off list for the same 12 months.
- Surge cushion: 20% transient burst capacity for first 90 days at 1.2x unit rate; aggregated monthly cap to prevent runaway spend.
- Credit: $25,000 one-time onboarding/scale credit applied if signed within 45 days.

Option B — Pay-as-you-go + buffer (flexible):
- Keep retainer; provide a dedicated burst pool for 90 days and a volume-tier discount for sustained usage growth.
- No price hold on list rate beyond current term; offer larger ramp discounts starting at 6 months if usage meets thresholds.

Operational notes:
- Overage rate will be list rate * 1.5 unless a pre-bought surge cushion is purchased.
- SLA credits tied to latency SLOs can be included in the SOW; typical language: up to 10% service credit for repeated SLO misses.

I've attached a short comparison doc that maps the financial tradeoffs and a straw-man SOW outline (SOW draft will be editable by procurement).

Attachments: SolarCog_Renewal_Comparison_Q3-10-01.pdf

If that looks useful, I'd like to schedule a 30-minute call with you, Ethan (procurement) and Monica (CS lead) to nail down target numbers. Proposed times: Wed 10/3 10:00-11:00 or Thu 10/4 15:00-16:00 PT.

Cheers,
David Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Thanks David — this is helpful. A few clarifying Qs from procurement: 
- For Option A, is the 10% discount on incremental capacity applied to the carded price or the blended rate? We prefer predictable unit economics so carded price alignment helps.
- Can the surge cushion be structured as a prepaid burst pool so we avoid punitive overage multipliers? If so, what's the crediting model?
- SLA credits — can you provide the exact clause language we can drop into our SOW? Procurement will also need an amortization schedule for the $25k credit (our finance team asks for visibility).

Ethan, please flag anything else we need on the legal/SOW side. We can do the Wed 10/3 10:00 slot if that still works for Redwood.

Regards,
Tanya
VP Product — SolarCog
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: david_kim@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: Tanya Rosales <tanya@solarcog.com>, procurement@solarcog.com, Ethan Moore <ethan@solarcog.com>
Date: Fri, 05 Oct 2028 16:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — capacity uplift and price hold

Team — jumping in to tighten the numbers for the call and make sure legal gets a redline-able artifact. Proposed firm terms to present: 

- Commit: 12-month firm baseline with 30% uplift from current average monthly commit (signed on Q4 effective date).
- Pricing: preserve today's effective blended unit rate for 12 months on the existing baseline; incremental commit (the 30% uplift) priced at 10% below list for the same 12 months.
- Surge insurance: pre-purchased burst pool equivalent to 20% of baseline capacity, available for 90 days post-go-live. Usage from the pool billed at 1.2x list and unused burst credit expires. This avoids the 1.5x overage multiplier if pool is purchased.
- SLA credits: standard clause (attached) — credit up to 10% of monthly invoice for repeated latency/SLO misses (three breaches in a 30-day rolling window). We'll put language in SOW.
- Credit amortization: $25,000 onboarding credit amortized over the first 6 invoices at $4,166.67/mo; if SolarCog accelerates payment terms (annual prepay), credit becomes $0 immediate on contract execution.

Attachments: SolarCog_MAAP_SOW_v3.docx

Next steps: David — get DocuSign-ready SOW with the language above; Monica — prepare a one-slide ops runbook showing how the burst pool is implemented and the visibility hooks in Redwood Console. Tanya/Ethan — procurement redline expected within 5 business days once SOW is delivered.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
